title: FRC - First Robotics
blurb: Where the collaborative-engineering bug first bit — programming and wiring a competition robot with FIRST Robotics.
body:
My first real experience building something technical alongside a team came in high school, competing in the FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) with team 3546, the Buc'n'gears. Designing and building a competition robot on a tight timeline, shoulder-to-shoulder with people from all kinds of backgrounds, was what first got me hooked on collaborative technical work.

I worked on the programming and electrical side of the team, writing the robot's control code in Java and handling its wiring. It was where I first learned to think in terms of methods and classes, and where I came to appreciate how much a project depends on a team that communicates well and pulls in the same direction.

By the time I graduated I had worked my way up to co-captain, leading the programming and electrical efforts and mentoring newer members — an early version of the technical leadership I have continued to grow into ever since.
